text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VIETNAM NEWS
-- Vietnam and Laos held talks to plan cooperation in the new year for the proper implementation of a border treaty signed in 1990.
-- Vietnam achieved the target set for coal production in 2000 three years ahead of schedule, turning out 10.9 million tonnes in 1996.
-- The Price Control Committee hopes to contain price increases to about seven to eight percent next year.
-- Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and two Japanese trading firms will build a telephone network in Vietnam at a cost of 21 billion yen ($184 million).

-- U.S.-based Business Software Alliance and the Software Publishers Association (SPA) say Vietnam has the highest software piracy rate in the world. Their survey put the piracy rate in Vietnam at 99 percent compared with 96 percent in China.
SAIGON TIMES DAILY
-- The government has begun collecting data for a feasibility study to build a 1,900-km (1,188-mile) North-South expressway linking Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.

-- There has been a strong shift in the area and structure of foreign direct investment in Vietnam over the past year. FDI in southern Vietnam has continued to increase, accounting for 64 percent of the nationwide foreign investment. However, big economic centres such as Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and Dong Nai have seen a far smaller share of the total than in previous years.
-- The temperature in Dalat fell to 5.4 degrees centigrade on Friday, the coldest recorded in the tourist resort city since 1975.
-- The Ho Chi Minh City Electricity Company plans to invest $26 million during 1997-98 on an electrification project for 43 suburban communes in the country's southern metropolis.

-- A $270-million project to dredge the heavily polluted eight-km (five-mile) Nhieu Loc-Thi Nghe canal is expected to begin next year, the vice director of the Ho Chi Minh City Service of Communications and Public Works said.
NHAN DAN
-- A state mourning ceremony for the former president of the National Liberation Front of South Vietnam and former acting president Nguyen Huu Tho was held in Ho Chi Minh city on Sunday.
-- The General Cement Company has produced 5.3 million tonnes of cement this year, a rise of 400,000 tonnes from the last year level.
-- Industrial output growth rate is expected to reach 14 percent in 1996.
HANOI MOI
-- The country's trade gap widened to $4 billion in 1996, with imports at $11 billion and exports at $7 billion.
SAIGON GIAI PHONG
-- The government has issued a directive to tighten control over alcohol smuggling.
DAU TU

-- State-run PetroVietnam has signed an agreement with British Petroleum and Norway's Statoil on gas exploitation in Lan Tay and Lan Do gas fields in Nam Con Son, which has estimated gas reserves of 57 billion cubic metre.
-- The government tourist department said the number of foreign visitors to Vietnam rose by 18 percent to 1.6 million in 1996. In 1995 the growth was 33 percent.
